newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gold to face resistance over $320.00.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gold to face resistance over $320.00.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Gold's technical background has improved this week leading analysts to forecast a possible test of resistance at $320.00 per ounce and above on Thursday.
The price had been firmed partially by short-covering against a heavy oversold ratio but sentiment remained extremely vulnerable, they said.
GOLD -

Support at around $315.00 per ounce for bullion held for the second day on Wednesday but was not to be trusted implicitly in a market still itching with tension after its plunge late last week, analysts said.
The announcement of by the Reserve Bank of Australia of the sale of 167 tonnes of gold from its reserves over the past six months took gold to its lowest levels in almost 12 years.

"With the technical indicators looking heavily oversold and a bullish flag possibly forming we could see a corrective bounce sooner rather than later," said broker Rudolf Wolff and Co's technical analyst Martin Squires.
On the Comex August contract that would mean a removal of resistance at $322.00-$325.00 before further progress was possible, he added.
Gold was still heavily oversold at an RSI of 21 suggesting more profit-taking and covering by the shorts had to come.

The dollar at a fresh 41-month high against the mark in early European dealings would put pressure on gold however and pressure from trade and speculative buying in the Far East markets also suggested gold would find the upside limited.
At 0745 GMT gold was indicated at $319.40/$319.90 compared with Wednesday's closing level at $317.90/$318.40.
SILVER -
Gains were held overnight after a visit to the $4.25 support level brought a bounce on Wednesday.
However, silver has not yet established a trend and has disappointed on the upside several times in the past few weeks making analysts wary. But the upside seems to be favoured.
"With the techncial indicators attempting to push up out of the oversold band (RSI of 28) and a bullish flag possibly forming, we await confirmation of a trend," said Squires.
Medium term resistance was expected at $4.57 and $4.62 before the more significant levels were encountered.
Silver was sitting on initial support on Thursday morning and a fall would take it to $4.28 then $4.22.
AT 0755 GMT silver was indicated at $4.34/$4.36 up two cents from Wednesday's closing level.
PLATINUM -
A base seemed to be forming around $395.00 following the break through the psychologically significant $400 level earlier this week.
Unlike gold and silver platinum was not oversold at an RSI of 39.
However phsycial factors were more likely to be significant than technical issues for platinum, analysts said.
Russian deliveries to Japan were expected to begin Thursday for the first time this year and their failure to arrive would probably spark a rally, they said.
The deliveries were now well discounted into the price and no immediate weakness was likely when they arrived in Tokyo, according to dealers.
However there was plenty of room on the downside in platinum before it got back to a more normal premium over gold of between $20-$50 from its current level of around $75.00, they said.
At 0800 GMT platinum was indicated at $395.00/$400, down about $2.50 from Wednesday's close.
--Brian Spoors London Newsroom +44 171 542 8058
